This item is the owner decision on mitigation.\n\n## Context (measured on papercup-vm-win, 2026-10-06)\npapercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/wsl_setup.rs ensure_wsl_networking_config (WI-3360) writes `[wsl2] networkingMode=mirrored` into the user's GLOBAL %USERPROFILE%\\.wslconfig when no networkingMode is set. Mirrored mode (WSL 2.7.11) installs `table ip filter chain WSLOUTPUT { hook output priority filter; meta mark set 0x1 }`, which overwrites every locally generated packet's mark, plus `ipproto tcp lookup 127` (127.0.0.1 via loopback0) ahead of `lookup local`. Result: in ANY distro, a ROOTFUL podman/netavark `-p 127.0.0.1:<port>` connect from Linux hangs (masquerade mark erased, so the SYN reaches the container from 127.0.0.1); once masquerade is restored, the reply is routed out loopback0 and resets. The same port answers from Windows. Our operator is unaffected (it binds 127.0.0.1 natively). Users' own rootful bridge publishes regress after our installer applies the setting.\n\nVerified workaround (test4, ~/p0-bench/wi10006715/test4.sh): own nft table `out` chain (filter output, priority filter+10) on `ip saddr 127.0.0.0/8 ct status dnat ct direction original` sets ct mark 0x40000 and re-asserts meta mark | 0x2000; `pre` chain (mangle prerouting) copies 0x40000 onto reply packets of ct-marked conns; `ip rule pref 0 fwmark 0x40000/0x40000 lookup local`. Linux side HTTP 200 x3, Windows side still 200, removal restores the hang. A naive `iif podman0 to 127/8 lookup local` rule fixes Linux but BREAKS the Windows side.\n\n## Decision needed (owner)\n(a) Keep auto-mirrored; the cost is now documented in wsl_setup.rs (done in WI-10006715).\n(b) Additionally install the origin-aware workaround from the runtime distro at boot. At 04:20:04 EDT it shows result=failed mode=wait reason=lock-timeout timeout_sec=900, then systemd: Main process exited, status=75/TEMPFAIL. The unit has stayed failed since (ActiveState=failed, InactiveEnterTimestamp 04:20:08 EDT), and the supervision alert lists it as a failed unit.\n\nWhy it matters: the timer is OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:00:00 with Persistent=true. Persistent only catches up a run missed while the timer was inactive. It does not re-run a run that started and failed. So one busy lock at 04:00 skips the cold home snapshot for the whole day. Today the lock was held by the hot sweep and db-dump traffic that EI-25211496463956189 dealt with.\n\nUnits: the repo copy apps/operator/scripts/systemd/kopia-home-snapshot.service matches the installed copy. It has no SuccessExitStatus=75 and no retry. The guard's own comment (kopia-backup-guard.sh, about line 139) says a scheduled cycle that did not run is retryable, not successful, and that scheduled units use SuccessExitStatus=75 to keep expected retries out of OnFailure. kopia-snapshots.service declares SuccessExitStatus=75; the home unit does not.\n\nProposed fix (not started): retry a TEMPFAIL'd daily run within the same day, for example Restart=on-failure + RestartForceExitStatus=75 + RestartSec=30min, with a start limit that covers a few hours. Alternatively, raise the wait timeout for this cold, once-a-day job. Keep 75 out of OnFailure alerts only while a retry is still pending. Add a unit-file contract test next to the existing apps/operator/scripts/__tests__/backup-*.test.ts for a plain store that is every top-level entry of `scratchRoot()` with `mtimeMs = statSync(<entry>).mtimeMs` (packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk.ts ~L426-430). It then `rmSync(entry, { recursive:true })` for each entry older than the floor.\n\nA directory's own mtime changes only when a DIRECT child is added/removed, so it lags deep writes:\n- `~/.papercusp/scratch/papercusp-workspace/` (the LIVE registered workspace root) showed top-level mtime 14:31 local while result-door spills were being written under it at 17:08 local. A prune with olderThanDays ≥ 1 run a day after the last new tool dir appeared would delete the whole live workspace root, including spills a recipient has not read yet.\n- An agent's scratch tree with an active deep writer (e.g. a PG datadir under `<dir>/pg-shared/`) has an old top-level mtime and would be deleted mid-run — the WI-10006512 incident class.\n\n## Exposure\nManual/explicit only today: `storage:prune` tool + `/api/agent-mcp/storage-prune` route, dry-run by default. `telemetry-retention` routine targets (`DEFAULT_RETENTION_TARGETS`) do NOT include 'scratch', but a routine trigger config could add it.\n\n## Proposed fix\nFor `store:'scratch'`, do not prune top-level entries by their own mtime. Delegate to scratch-gc's rules (WI-10006512): registered workspace roots are pruned at RUN-DIR granularity (`<ws>/<tool>/<runId>` by run mtime); unregistered roots only when marker-proven + quiet (newest mtime in tree) + no open writer/cwd; unmarked entries never. Regression test in packages/operator-core/lib/storage/prune.test.ts: a live workspace root with an old top-level mtime but a fresh deep spill survives `olderThanDays:1`; an unmarked agent dir survives.\n\n[self-imposed] residue of WI-10006512; not Fix: install WALinuxAgent (CentOS Stream 9 AppStream), gate the waagent unit off non-Azure firmware with a ConditionFirmware drop-in (same pattern as papercusp-amazon-ssm-agent-ec2-only.conf and the new papercusp-google-guest-agent-gce-only.conf), and check that its provisioning does not fight cloud-init or the papercusp host-prepare service. Then remove the WALinuxAgent exemption from packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/bootc-guest-tool-contracts.test.ts. Azure is outside plan aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01, so this is lower priority than Read /mnt/backup/db-dumps/STATUS.json (ok / failed[] / lastSuccessEpoch) and /mnt/backup/db-dumps/db-backup.log.\n 2. A specific DB's dump is failing validation: db-backup.sh only renames a dump into place after pg_restore -l passes, so a per-DB 'FAIL' in db-backup.log means the archive was unreadable or the dump errored — read the actual pg_dump error there. DO NOT blindly raise PC_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SEC without reading it.\n 3. An orphaned pg_dump is holding locks (the EI-10730 knock-on): check for a pg_dump backend older than its timeout (SELECT pid, application_name, backend_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'pg_dump%'). db-backup.sh tags its own dumps PGAPPNAME=pcbackup and reaps foreign ones; a lingering 'pg_dump%' backend is a legacy/manual dump.\n 4. Disk full on the backup volume: df -h /mnt/backup/db-dumps\n\nAn orphaned/stuck dump is not just a dead backup — it holds AccessShareLock on ~593 tables, which starves every migration's ACCESS
